assistant.raw: Core insight: this is not a prompt problem, it is a data loading strategy problem. The primary issue is eager loading of large artifacts, especially the lugs file. Key fixes: 1) Eliminate full lug loading at startup, replace with selective loading. 2) Introduce lug index to summarize and reference full records. 3) Split WAI-State into runtime vs rarely used. 4) Convert skills into callable fragments. 5) Introduce session slim mode. 6) Replace raw history loading with signals layer. Core architectural shift: Memory should be accessible, not preloaded.

user.raw: Do all three and Ill have it consume this track to understand our thinking and design the roadmap to implement. I love the idea of squeezing the value out of each session.

assistant.raw: Three-part package designed: 1) Lazy-load native wake-up protocol - Cold boot loads only runtime state, prompt, lug index, signals summary. Classify task into capture_only, local_task, continuation_task, stateful_governance_task, closeout_task. Hydrate only minimal relevant data per classification. Never load full lugs or archives by default. 2) Lug index schema - Introduce WAI-LugIndex.jsonl as lightweight lookup layer. Split full lugs into active and archive files. Load only matching lugs based on tags, project, status. Archive completed lugs and keep index reference. 3) Context budget governor - Define budget tiers: green, yellow, orange, red. Classify context into Tier A (essential), B (useful), C (reference). Compress or eject based on thresholds. Prefer summaries and signals over raw data. Implementation roadmap: Phase 1 split lugs and state, introduce index. Phase 2 selective hydration. Phase 3 governor enforcement. Phase 4 session value extraction via signals. Final principle: Context is a budget, not a landfill.
